newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait seen gradually selling Santa Fe holding.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait seen gradually selling Santa Fe holding.

text.p: Kuwait could gradually sell most of its wholly-owned Santa Fe oil firm to focus more on boosting domestic and foreign oil refining capacity, executives said on Monday.

"The sale of the entire company depends on the market," said a senior banker familiar with Kuwait's plan to shed in June 30 million Santa Fe Drilling shares, about 30 percent of the firm, for around $760 million.
"The market is hot now and oil prices are up, making the offering attractive," he told Reuters.
Bankers said state oil arm Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) was expected to offer a second tranch of its Santa Fe stake once prices stabilise after the initial public offering (IPO).
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission IPO will involve the sale of 24 million shares mainly to investors in the United States and six million abroad by about a dozen underwriters.

National Bank of Kuwait, the country's largest bank, and the Kuwait-based Gulf Investment Corp (GIC) are the oil-rich region's sole underwriters who will seek institutional investors and high-powered private banking customers.
KPC "wants to concentrate more on the downstream which makes more sense. The strategy now is different, it is more focused and more clear," said one banker.

"Kuwait has the commodity, it needs the markets," another said of plans to invest in Asian refineries, boost the domestic refining capacity beyond 895,000 barrels per day and further develop the local petrochemicals industry.
Kuwait, which operates a downstream network in Europe, has joint venture refinery plans in Pakistan and India and is studying prospects in Indonesia, Thailand and elsewhere.

Bankers said Kuwait's general policy to diversify foreign investments away from holding proportionally large stakes in any single firm, mainly oil companies, was prudent, including cutting its stake in May in British Petroleum Plc by three percent to 6.3 percent.

The $2 billion BP sale enjoyed a sovereign tax immunity as the shares were owned by the sovereign the Kuwait Investment Office, bankers said. Kuwait is a major global investor with some $40 billion invested abroad.
But Santa Fe, which has shown a profit in recent years, could be subject to U.S. taxes although bankers say accumulated losses could spare KPC making large payments.
They expect Kuwait to succeed in selling the shares at between $24 and $27 each.
Underwriters for the offering are led by Goldman, Sachs & Co and Credit Suisse First Boston, Merrill Lynch & Co and Morgan Stanley & Co.
"I think it will sell well and there will be no problem achieving the target," said a banker close to the IPO.
Earlier a Kuwait watchdog body had said KPC paid twice the market price, $2.5 billion, for the 1981 purchase of Santa Fe which made losses of $2.89 billion between 1981 and 1990.

Kuwait has so far sold Santa Fe's CF Braun and Santa Fe Minerals' operations in North and South America -- parts of that firm were taken over by other KPC firms. In December Kuwait sold Santa Fe North Sea exploration to Norway's Saga for $1.23 billion.
The remaining drilling company, the core business for Santa Fe when it was formed in 1946, has offshore and onshore interests in some 15 countries.
